stories.primary_headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives

primary_source.headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives
primary_source.content: Srinagar: Jammu and Kashmir Police have booked the wife of a serving Army officer for alleged espionage-related activities involving foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, with investigators examining research papers she allegedly prepared on sensitive defence and geopolitical issues.The woman, a freelance researcher from Telangana, has not been arrested, and a preliminary inquiry has not established that she shared sensitive information, official sources said on Sunday.The case was registered at Gandhi Nagar police station on Friday under the Official Secrets Act, 1923, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).She was questioned by a Deputy Superintendent of Police-rank officer following the registration of the FIR, according to a PTI report.'Espionage Alert': UK accuses China of using academics to spy on AI and other tech researchInvestigators are examining allegations that the woman was tasked with preparing analytical papers on subjects including Line of Control (LoC) dynamics in Jammu and Kashmir, critical infrastructure projects in Arunachal Pradesh and drone deployment, sources said.The assignments allegedly involved individuals linked to Chinese intelligence operatives, they said.According to reports, the woman is well-qualified, undertook an IT internship with the United Nations in 2023 and currently works as a freelance researcher.The investigation is seeking to establish the nature of her contacts with foreign entities and whether any information or material was communicated to them.The allegations have not been independently established, and police have not publicly detailed the evidence recovered or confirmed whether any classified documents were involved.The investigation comes months after a Delhi court acquitted five accused in a separate espionage case registered in 2015.The accused, including serving and former security personnel, had faced charges under the Official Secrets Act over allegations of passing information about Army and Border Security Force deployments in Jammu and Kashmir to Pakistan-based intelligence operatives.In its May 20, 2026, judgment, the court found that the prosecution had failed to establish that the documents allegedly recovered were classified official records and that protected information had been communicated to enemy agents. All five accused were acquitted.

stories.primary_headline: One month of IIT Bombay student's death: No arrests yet; protest continues

primary_source.headline: One month of IIT Bombay student's death: No arrests yet; protest continues
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Exactly a month after Sahil Wakode, a student of Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay died by suicide, students and activists staged a protest outside the institute’s Powai campus on Sunday, however, police dispersed the mob and detained several of them.The parents of Sahil—Ravindra Wakode and Sonali Wakode—too were part of the protests.&nbsp;On 18 September, Sahil (20), a second-year student from Energy Science and Engineering Department, was caught allegedly using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination. However, his body was later found in his hostel room.&nbsp;The case is being investigated by the&nbsp;Crime Branch-CID, which has taken over investigations from the Powai police station.&nbsp;Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by policeThe parents are demanding action and arrest of&nbsp; Prof Shireesh Kedare, the Director of&nbsp; Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay and Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, a faculty member of the premier institute’s Energy Science and Engineering Department.Meanwhile, the Congress once again backed the parents and said that it will ensure that Sahil Wakode gets justice. Sahil Wakode, a backward-class student at the IIT Mumbai institution, did not commit suicide; it was "an institutional murder."“Even though a month has passed since this incident, no action has been taken against anyone yet. In the past 13 months, 4 students in this institution have died by suicide. After Sahil's death, students in the institution are protesting, and the police are committing atrocities against them, beating them. On whose orders are the police committing atrocities in the institution's premises? All these things must stop. An inquiry must be conducted quickly, and strict action must be taken against those responsible for Sahil's murder,” said Mumbai Congress president and MP Prof Varsha Gaikwad.&nbsp;“RSS ideology has infiltrated this prestigious IIT institution, and this is not good for the education sector. Keep educational institutions away from political ideologies,” she added.&nbsp;A delegation from the All India Independent Scheduled Castes Association arrived at the IIT Bombay gates around noon, seeking to pay respects to Sahil.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: Govt asks Meta to ensure its recommendation systems don't expose users to a limited set of narratives

primary_source.headline: Govt asks Meta to ensure its recommendation systems don't expose users to a limited set of narratives
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The government has asked Meta, owner of Instagram and Facebook, to ensure that its recommendation systems do not result in "disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives", and to step up checks on content that could cause public disorder or incite violence or other unlawful activity.The advisory by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), dated October 10, asked Meta to undertake appropriate measures to provide adequate context in relation to photographs, videos, graphics, or other content depicting ongoing public events, particularly where the authenticity, date, location or circumstances of such content may not be readily apparent to users. Quick summary - click for full detailsConcise summary of key highlightsGovt asks Meta to ensure its recommendation systems do not disproportionate expose users to a limited set of narrativesIn one lineIndia's IT Ministry has directed Meta to prevent its algorithms from disproportionately amplifying limited narratives or misleading content during public events.Key highlights• Government Issues Advisory to MetaThe Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology issued an advisory on October 10 requiring Meta to review its content-ranking and recommendation systems.• Concerns Over Narrative BiasAgency reports indicated that Meta's algorithms were disproportionately favouring specific types of content and exposing users to a limited set of narratives.• Crackdown on Misleading ContentMeta has been instructed to curb the spread of out-of-context visuals, manipulated media, and unverified claims regarding public-order situations.• Criticism From Digital Rights GroupsThe Internet Freedom Foundation criticised the advisory as a continuing censorship directive that lacks explicit grounding in the IT Act or rules.Key statisticsOctober 10Advisory issuance date53 lakh piecesChild sexual exploitation content removed in IndiaProcessed with AI. Reviewed by DH Digital Team.Although the advisory does not identify any specific incident that prompted its issuance, it comes amid protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition parties in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.In the advisory seen by PTI, Meta has also been asked to review its recommendation and content-ranking mechanisms to ensure that potentially misleading, manipulated or out-of-context content is not disproportionately amplified or repeatedly recommended to users."...ensure that recommendation systems do not result in disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives, and endeavour to provide appropriate diversity of relevant and credible information," it said while seeking the strengthening of mechanisms for rapid identification, review and escalation of content, which is gaining significant reach through recommendation systems and has the potential to cause widespread public confusion, apprehension, violence or disturbance of public order.Govt advises social media firms to swiftly act on protests related unlawful postsWhen contacted, IT Ministry sources said the ministry had reports from agencies that Meta platforms were not promoting all narratives equally, with their algorithms appearing to favour one kind of content over others.MeitY, in its advisory, has also told Meta to ensure timely cooperation with law enforcement and other authorised government agencies, including furnishing information or assistance in accordance with applicable law and within the timelines prescribed under the IT Rules, 2021.It said the ministry has noticed that certain content relating to ongoing public events was being "prominently displayed and recommended to users" through platforms operated by Meta.Such content includes videos, images, statements and static graphics on public-order and law-and-order situations.The ministry said such material, when shown without adequate context or amplified disproportionately, "may contribute to public confusion, apprehension and disturbance of public order and social tranquillity".Citing the Information Technology Act, 2000, the advisory said Meta, as an intermediary, must observe due diligence under the IT Rules, 2021. These rules require intermediaries to inform users about prohibited information, including content likely to cause public disorder or incite a cognisable offence relating to public order.MeitY asked Meta to pay particular attention to content that presents old, unrelated or selectively edited visuals as current events, and content with unverified or misleading claims about emergency, restrictions, police action or other official measures.Meta removes 53 lakh pieces of child sexual exploitation content in IndiaIt also flagged audio-visual material on law-and-order situations without adequate context, content likely to incite violence or other unlawful activity, and content being disproportionately amplified despite being potentially misleading.The advisory outlined six specific asks for Meta. These include measures to identify and address content under the IT Rules, and a review of its recommendation and ranking systems so that misleading, manipulated or out-of-context content is not "disproportionately amplified or repeatedly recommended to users".The ministry emphasised that its advisory is intended to facilitate responsible dissemination and recommendation of information while respecting lawful expression and legitimate public discourse."Meta is advised to ensure that any action taken pursuant to this advisory is consistent with the Information Technology Act, 2000, the IT Rules, 2021, and other applicable laws," it said.The social media giant has been advised to take the necessary measures "with immediate effect" and apprise the ministry of the action taken.Apar Gupta, Founder Director of Internet Freedom Foundation, a digital rights advocacy group, said that while the advisory is not legally binding, it amounts to a "continuing censorship directive".MeitY must withdraw this advisory forthwith, and Meta must publicly disclose every takedown and every act of downranking carried out under it, he said."Even this advisory, which contains phrases like content 'without adequate context' and periods of 'heightened public-order sensitivity ', is not tied to any provision of the IT Act or the IT Rules," he said.
